metadata.title: Are Transformers universal approximators of sequence-to-sequence functions?
metadata.authors: Chulhee Yun, Srinadh Bhojanapalli, Ankit Singh Rawat, Sashank J. Reddi, Sanjiv Kumar

nodes.name: Transformer block
nodes.statement: A Transformer block $t^{h,m,r}: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ is the composition $\mathrm{FF} \circ \mathrm{Attn}$ of a multi-head self-attention layer and a token-wise feed-forward layer, each with a skip connection.
nodes.statement_clean: A Transformer block is a sequence-to-sequence map composed of a self-attention layer and a token-wise feed-forward layer, both with residual connections.

nodes.name: Transformer network class $\mathcal{T}^{h,m,r}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{T}^{h,m,r} \defeq \{ g: \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \mid g \text{ is a composition of Transformer blocks } t^{h,m,r} \}$, where $h$ is the number of heads, $m$ the head size, and $r$ the FF hidden width.

nodes.name: Permutation equivariance
nodes.statement: A function $f : \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ is permutation equivariant if $f(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{P}) = f(\mathbf{X})\mathbf{P}$ for every permutation matrix $\mathbf{P}$.

nodes.name: Target class $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$ is the class of all continuous permutation-equivariant functions $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ with compact support, where continuity is with respect to the entry-wise $\ell^p$ norm, $1 \leq p < \infty$.

nodes.name: Distance $\mathsf{d}_p$ between functions
nodes.statement: For $f_1, f_2 : \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, $\mathsf{d}_p(f_1,f_2) \defeq \big( \int \| f_1(\mathbf{X}) - f_2(\mathbf{X}) \|_p^p \, d\mathbf{X} \big)^{1/p}$.

nodes.name: Transformer class with positional encodings $\mathcal{T}^{h,m,r}_{\mathrm{P}}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{T}^{h,m,r}_{\mathrm{P}} \defeq \{ g_{\mathrm{P}}(\mathbf{X}) = g(\mathbf{X} + \mathbf{E}) \mid g \in \mathcal{T}^{h,m,r}, \mathbf{E} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \}$, where $\mathbf{E}$ is a (trainable) positional-encoding matrix.

nodes.name: Target class $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{CD}}$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{CD}}$ is the set of all continuous functions mapping a compact domain $\mathbb{D} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ to $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$, without the permutation-equivariance restriction.

nodes.name: Contextual mapping
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ be finite. A map $q : \mathcal{L} \to \mathbb{R}^{1 \times n}$ is a contextual mapping if (i) for every $\mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{L}$ the $n$ entries of $q(\mathbf{L})$ are distinct and (ii) for $\mathbf{L} \neq \mathbf{L}'$ in $\mathcal{L}$, all entries of $q(\mathbf{L})$ and $q(\mathbf{L}')$ are distinct.
nodes.statement_clean: A contextual mapping assigns a unique scalar to every (token, context) pair, capturing the entire input context.

nodes.name: Piece-wise constant class $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta)$
nodes.statement: $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta) \defeq \{ f : \mathbf{X} \mapsto \sum_{\mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{G}_\delta} \mathbf{A}_\mathbf{L} \mathbb{1}\{\mathbf{X} \in \mathcal{S}_\mathbf{L}\} \mid f \text{ permutation equivariant}, \mathbf{A}_\mathbf{L} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \}$, where $\mathcal{G}_\delta = \{0,\delta,\dots,1-\delta\}^{d \times n}$ and $\mathcal{S}_\mathbf{L}$ is the cube of width $\delta$ anchored at $\mathbf{L}$.

nodes.name: Modified Transformer class $\overline{\mathcal{T}}^{h,m,r}$
nodes.statement: $\overline{\mathcal{T}}^{h,m,r}$ replaces softmax $\sigma$ with hardmax $\sigma_\mathrm{H}$ and ReLU with an activation $\phi \in \Phi$, where $\Phi$ is the set of piecewise-linear functions with at most three pieces, at least one of which is constant.

nodes.name: Extended grid $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta$ and quantized subset $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta \defeq \{-\delta^{-nd}, 0, \delta, \dots, 1-\delta\}^{d \times n}$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta \defeq \{ \mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{G}_\delta \mid \mathbf{L}_{:,i} \neq \mathbf{L}_{:,j} \text{ for all } i \neq j \}$ (grid points with all-distinct columns).

nodes.name: Selective shift operation $\Psi$
nodes.statement: $\Psi(\mathbf{Z}; b, b')_{1,j} = \max_k \mathbf{Z}_{1,k} - \min_k \mathbf{Z}_{1,k}$ if $b < \mathbf{Z}_{1,j} < b'$, else $0$. Realized by two attention heads of size $1$ with $\sigma_\mathrm{H}$. The attention layer $\mathbf{Z} \mapsto \mathbf{Z} + \Psi(\mathbf{Z};b,b')$ shifts only entries inside $(b,b')$.

nodes.name: Self-attention layer
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{Attn}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \sum_{i=1}^h \mathbf{W}_O^i \mathbf{W}_V^i \mathbf{X} \cdot \sigma\big[(\mathbf{W}_K^i \mathbf{X})^T \mathbf{W}_Q^i \mathbf{X}\big]$.

nodes.name: Token-wise feed-forward layer
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{FF}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathrm{Attn}(\mathbf{X}) + \mathbf{W}_2 \, \mathrm{ReLU}\!\big(\mathbf{W}_1 \mathrm{Attn}(\mathbf{X}) + \mathbf{b}_1 \mathbf{1}_n^T\big) + \mathbf{b}_2 \mathbf{1}_n^T$.

nodes.name: Bi-linear projection layer
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{BProj}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{W}_O \cdot \mathbf{X} \cdot \mathbf{W}_P$.

nodes.name: Depth-wise separable convolution layer
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{SepConv}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{W}_O (\mathbf{X} \ast \mathbf{W}_C)$ with $\mathbf{W}_C \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times k}$ and $(\mathbf{X} \ast \mathbf{W}_C)_{i,:} = \mathbf{X}_{i,:} \ast (\mathbf{W}_C)_{i,:}$.

nodes.name: Permutation equivariance of Transformer block
nodes.statement: A Transformer block $t^{h,m,r}$ defines a permutation-equivariant map from $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ to $\mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$.

nodes.name: Universal approximation of permutation-equivariant seq-to-seq functions (Theorem 1)
nodes.statement: Let $1 \leq p < \infty$ and $\epsilon > 0$. For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$ there exists a Transformer network $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(f,g) \leq \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Universal approximation of arbitrary seq-to-seq functions with positional encodings (Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: Let $1 \leq p < \infty$ and $\epsilon > 0$. For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{CD}}$ there exists a Transformer network $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}_{\mathrm{P}}$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(f,g) \leq \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Modified Transformer approximates piece-wise constant class (Proposition 1)
nodes.statement: For each $\overline{f} \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta)$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, there exists $\overline{g} \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(\overline{f}, \overline{g}) = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Piece-wise constant approximation of $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$ (Lemma 1)
nodes.statement: For any $f \in \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PE}}$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, there exists $\delta^* > 0$ and $\overline{f} \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta^*)$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(f, \overline{f}) \leq \epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Modified Transformer approximated by original Transformer (Lemma 9)
nodes.statement: For each $\overline{g} \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ and $1 \leq p < \infty$, there exists $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(\overline{g}, g) \leq \epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Quantization by feed-forward layers (Lemma 2)
nodes.statement: There exists a function $g_{\mathrm{q}} : \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathcal{G}^+_\delta$ composed of $d/\delta + d$ token-wise feed-forward layers ($r=1$) with activations in $\Phi$ that applies the scalar quantization $g_{\mathrm{q}}^{\mathrm{ent}}$ entry-wise; in particular $g_{\mathrm{q}}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{L}$ for $\mathbf{X} \in \mathcal{S}_\mathbf{L}$.
assumptions: Scalar quantization $g_{\mathrm{q}}^{\mathrm{ent}}(t) = k\delta$ if $k\delta \leq t < (k+1)\delta$, else $-\delta^{-nd}$
conclusions: $\exists \, g_{\mathrm{q}}$ realized by $d/\delta + d$ FF layers with $\Phi$-activations that quantizes inputs entry-wise to $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta$

nodes.name: Self-attention realizes a contextual mapping (Lemma 3)
nodes.statement: Assume $n \geq 2$ and $\delta^{-1} \geq 2$. There exists $g_{\mathrm{c}} : \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ composed of $\delta^{-d}+1$ self-attention layers ($h=2, m=1$) using $\sigma_\mathrm{H}$, a vector $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and constants $0 < t_l < t_r$, such that $q(\mathbf{L}) \defeq \mathbf{u}^T g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})$ has distinct entries on $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$, separates non-permutation pairs, lies in $[t_l,t_r]$ on $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$, and lies outside $[t_l,t_r]$ on $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$.
conclusions: $\exists \, g_{\mathrm{c}}$ of $\delta^{-d}+1$ attention layers ($h=2, m=1, \sigma_\mathrm{H}$), $\mathbf{u} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and $0 < t_l < t_r$ such that $q(\mathbf{L}) = \mathbf{u}^T g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})$ implements a permutation-equivariant contextual mapping on $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$ inside $[t_l,t_r]$ and sends $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$ outside $[t_l,t_r]$

nodes.name: Function-value mapping by feed-forward layers (Lemma 4)
nodes.statement: There exists $g_{\mathrm{v}} : \mathbb{R}^{d \times n} \to \mathbb{R}^{d \times n}$ composed of $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ token-wise feed-forward layers ($r=1$, activations in $\Phi$) acting columnwise as $g_{\mathrm{v}}^{\mathrm{tkn}}$, with $g_{\mathrm{v}}^{\mathrm{tkn}}(g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})_{:,j}) = (\mathbf{A}_\mathbf{L})_{:,j}$ for $\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$ and $\mathbf{0}_d$ otherwise.
conclusions: $\exists \, g_{\mathrm{v}}$ of $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ token-wise FF layers that maps $g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})$ to the desired piecewise-constant value $\mathbf{A}_\mathbf{L}$ on $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$ and to $\mathbf{0}$ on $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$

nodes.name: Bounds and bijectivity of column-id map (Sublemma 1)
nodes.statement: After $n$ selective shift operations, $\widetilde{l}_n = \mathbf{u}^T \widetilde{\mathbf{L}}_{:,n}$ satisfies $\delta^{-(n-1)d+1}(\delta^{-d}-1) \leq \widetilde{l}_n \leq \delta^{-nd+1}(\delta^{-d}-1) - \delta(\delta^{-d}-1)^2$, and the map $[l_1, \dots, l_n] \mapsto \widetilde{l}_n$ is one-to-one on increasing tuples.
conclusions: The stated lower and upper bounds on $\widetilde{l}_n$ hold

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (universal approximation)
nodes.statement: Three-stage approximation: approximate $f$ by piece-wise constant $\overline{f}$ (Lemma 1), approximate $\overline{f}$ by modified Transformer $\overline{g} \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ (Proposition 1), then approximate $\overline{g}$ by $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ (Lemma 9). Triangle inequality gives $\mathsf{d}_p(f,g) \leq 2\epsilon/3 + O(\delta^{d/p})$, and $\delta$ small enough yields $\leq \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2 (positional encodings)
nodes.statement: Repeat the proof of Theorem 1 with positional encoding $\mathbf{E}$ that shifts column $j$ entries into $[j-1, j]^d$, removing column duplicates and obviating permutation equivariance. Quantization, contextual mapping, and value mapping are adapted accordingly.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 1 (permutation equivariance of Transformer block)
nodes.statement: Use $(\mathbf{W}_K^i \mathbf{X}\mathbf{P})^T (\mathbf{W}_Q^i \mathbf{X}\mathbf{P}) = \mathbf{P}^T (\mathbf{W}_K^i \mathbf{X})^T (\mathbf{W}_Q^i \mathbf{X}) \mathbf{P}$ and $\sigma[\mathbf{P}^T \mathbf{S} \mathbf{P}] = \mathbf{P}^T \sigma[\mathbf{S}] \mathbf{P}$, yielding $\mathrm{Attn}(\mathbf{X}\mathbf{P}) = \mathrm{Attn}(\mathbf{X})\mathbf{P}$. Token-wise FF inherits equivariance from columnwise application of ReLU.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: Compose $\overline{g} = g_{\mathrm{v}} \circ g_{\mathrm{c}} \circ g_{\mathrm{q}}$ from Lemmas 2-4. On $\bigcup_{\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta} \mathcal{S}_\mathbf{L}$, $\overline{g}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{A}_\mathbf{L} = \overline{f}(\mathbf{X})$; elsewhere both equal $\mathbf{0}$ except on a set of measure $O(\delta^d)$, giving $\mathsf{d}_p(\overline{f}, \overline{g}) = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3 (contextual mapping)
nodes.statement: Stack $(1/\delta)^d$ selective-shift attention layers sweeping the column-ids of $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{L}$, then a global-shift attention layer. Case-analysis over $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$, $\mathcal{G}_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$, and $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta \setminus \mathcal{G}_\delta$ verifies all four properties.

nodes.name: Step 1: piece-wise constant approximation
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 1 to find $\overline{f} \in \overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\mathrm{PE}}(\delta)$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(f, \overline{f}) \leq \epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Step 2: modified Transformer approximation
nodes.statement: Use Proposition 1 to obtain $\overline{g} \in \overline{\mathcal{T}}^{2,1,1}$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(\overline{f}, \overline{g}) = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Step 3: original Transformer approximation
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 9 to find $g \in \mathcal{T}^{2,1,4}$ with $\mathsf{d}_p(\overline{g}, g) \leq \epsilon/3$.

nodes.name: Conclude via triangle inequality
nodes.statement: $\mathsf{d}_p(f,g) \leq \mathsf{d}_p(f,\overline{f}) + \mathsf{d}_p(\overline{f},\overline{g}) + \mathsf{d}_p(\overline{g},g) \leq 2\epsilon/3 + O(\delta^{d/p})$. Choose $\delta$ small enough so the bound is $\leq \epsilon$.

nodes.name: Quantize input via FF stack
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 2: $g_{\mathrm{q}}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{L}$ for $\mathbf{X} \in \mathcal{S}_\mathbf{L}$ and $g_{\mathrm{q}}(\mathbf{X})$ has a $-\delta^{-nd}$ coordinate when $\mathbf{X}$ leaves $[0,1]^{d \times n}$.

nodes.name: Apply contextual mapping by attention
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 3: $g_{\mathrm{c}}$ sends $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$ to a permutation-equivariant contextual map inside $[t_l,t_r]$ and sends the rest of $\mathcal{G}^+_\delta$ outside.

nodes.name: Map context to function values via FF stack
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 4: $g_{\mathrm{v}}$ maps $g_{\mathrm{c}}(\mathbf{L})$ columnwise to $\mathbf{A}_\mathbf{L}$ on $\widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$ and to $\mathbf{0}$ elsewhere; the missing region has measure $O(\delta^d)$.

nodes.name: Bound the $\mathsf{d}_p$ error
nodes.statement: Since $\overline{f}$ is bounded by $B$ on $[0,1]^{d \times n}$ and $\overline{g}$ matches $\overline{f}$ outside a set of measure $O(\delta^d)$, $\mathsf{d}_p(\overline{f}, \overline{g}) \leq (B^p \delta^d)^{1/p} = O(\delta^{d/p})$.

nodes.name: Define column-id $\mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{L}_{:,j}$
nodes.statement: Set $\mathbf{u} = (1, \delta^{-1}, \dots, \delta^{-d+1})$. Then $\mathbf{L}_{:,j} \mapsto \mathbf{u}^T \mathbf{L}_{:,j}$ is a bijection from $\{0,\delta,\dots,1-\delta\}^d$ onto $[0:\delta:\delta^{-d+1}-\delta]$, and any column with a $-\delta^{-nd}$ entry maps to a strictly negative value.

nodes.name: Construct selective-shift attention layer
nodes.statement: Build $\Psi(\mathbf{Z};b,b')$ from two hardmax attention heads of size $1$; $\mathbf{Z} \mapsto \mathbf{Z} + \Psi(\mathbf{Z};b,b')$ shifts entries with column-id in $(b,b')$ by $\max - \min$ and leaves the others fixed.

nodes.name: Sweep selective shifts over $[0:\delta:\delta^{-d+1}-\delta]$
nodes.statement: Stack $(1/\delta)^d$ attention layers $\delta^{-d}\Psi(\cdot; l-\delta/2, l+\delta/2)$ in increasing order of $l$, applying selective shifts to all column-ids successively.

nodes.name: Case 1: $\mathbf{L} \in \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$
nodes.statement: Sort column-ids $l_1 < \dots < l_n$. The $j$-th shift updates $\widetilde{l}_j = l_j + \sum_{k=1}^{j-1} \delta^{-kd}(l_{j-k}-l_{j-k+1}) + \delta^{-jd}(l_n-l_1)$, with $\widetilde{l}_1 < \widetilde{l}_2 < \dots < \widetilde{l}_n$ by Sublemma 1.

nodes.name: Case 2: $\mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{G}_\delta \setminus \widetilde{\mathcal{G}}_\delta$ (duplicate columns)
nodes.statement: With $n' < n$ distinct column-ids, the upper bound $\widetilde{l}_n \leq \delta^{-n'd+1}(\delta^{-d}-1) - \delta(\delta^{-d}-1)^2 < \delta^{-(n-1)d+1}(\delta^{-d}-1)$ shows $\widetilde{l}_n$ is strictly below Case 1 values.

nodes.name: Case 3: $\mathbf{L} \in \mathcal{G}^+_\delta \setminus \mathcal{G}_\delta$ (negative entries)
nodes.statement: Negative column-ids never get shifted upward; the global-shift layer pushes them further negative or pushes positive ids past $\delta^{-(2n+2)d+1} > t_r$, so all entries land outside $[t_l,t_r]$.

nodes.name: Global shift and verification of properties
nodes.statement: Append a final attention layer $\delta^{-(n+1)d}\psi(\cdot;0)$ that adds $\delta^{-(n+1)d}\widetilde{l}_n$ to each first-row entry. Disjoint intervals across distinct $\widetilde{l}_n$ then give Properties 1-4 of Lemma 3.

nodes.name: Bi-linear projection layer ($\mathrm{BProj}$)
nodes.statement: Layer $\mathrm{BProj}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{W}_O \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W}_P$ that uses a sequence-length-dependent right projection $\mathbf{W}_P$ to densify sparse token differences, providing a 'pair-wise contextual mapping'.

nodes.name: Depth-wise separable convolution layer ($\mathrm{SepConv}$)
nodes.statement: Layer $\mathrm{SepConv}(\mathbf{X}) = \mathbf{X} + \mathbf{W}_O (\mathbf{X} \ast \mathbf{W}_C)$ that convolves each input dimension with its own filter of size $k$; parameters are independent of the sequence length.

nodes.name: Average attention baseline
nodes.statement: Replaces the softmax score matrix in $\mathrm{Attn}$ with the constant matrix $\frac{1}{n}\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^T$, so every token receives the same average of value projections.

nodes.name: I am happy / I am Bob context illustration
nodes.statement: Two sentences $\mathbf{X} = [\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{I}, \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{am}, \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{happy}]$ and $\widetilde{\mathbf{X}} = [\mathbf{v}_\mathrm{I}, \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{am}, \mathbf{v}_\mathrm{Bob}]$ illustrate that the embedding of `I' must differ across contexts, motivating the contextual-mapping definition.

nodes.name: BERT-base hybrid models on SQuAD and MNLI
nodes.statement: Replacing the first $1$-$2$ self-attention layers of $\mathrm{BERT}_{\mathrm{BASE}}$ (12 layers) with $\mathrm{SepConv}$ improves SQuAD F1/EM and MNLI accuracy; replacing more layers degrades performance, suggesting attention plays roles beyond contextual mapping.

nodes.name: Standalone replacement architectures vs Transformer (Table 1)
nodes.statement: Standalone average-attention, $\mathrm{BProj}$, $\mathrm{SepConv}$, and Transformer baselines reach MNLI accuracies $66\%$, $72.3\%$, $73\%$, and $78.2\%$ respectively at large batch size; average attention's collapse confirms the tasks are non-trivial.

nodes.name: Tightness of construction
nodes.statement: The Theorem 1 construction uses $O(n(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ Transformer blocks with $O(d)$ parameters each, totalling $O(dn(1/\delta)^{dn}/n!)$ parameters. This matches the information-theoretic lower bound for memorizing piecewise-constant permutation-equivariant functions and beats the residual-network bound $O(dn(1/\delta)^{dn})$ of Lin & Jegelka.

nodes.name: Exponential depth in dimension is unavoidable
nodes.statement: Without smoothness assumptions, approximating arbitrary continuous functions on cubes requires memorizing $(\text{output dim}) \times (\text{number of cubes})/n!$ values, so the exponential dependence on $dn$ in the parameter count is unavoidable in the worst case.

nodes.name: Universal approximation versus Turing completeness
nodes.statement: Universal approximation (functions on a continuum) and Turing completeness (computation on discrete formal languages) are distinct concepts: P\'erez et al.\ 2019 prove infinite-precision Transformers are Turing complete and Dehghani et al.\ 2018 disprove it in finite precision, and neither result implies universal approximation.

nodes.name: Universal approximation by width-$(d+1)$ deep ReLU networks (cited)
nodes.statement: A fully-connected ReLU network with input dimension $d$, width $d+1$, and unbounded depth is a universal approximator of scalar-valued continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.origin_citation: Lu, Pu, Wang, Hu & Wang 2017; Hanin & Sellke 2017

nodes.name: ResNet universal approximation with one neuron per block (cited)
nodes.statement: A residual network with a single hidden neuron per residual block is a universal approximator of scalar-valued continuous functions, given unbounded depth.

nodes.name: Classical universal approximation theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: Given unbounded width, a one-hidden-layer feed-forward neural network can approximate any continuous function with compact support to arbitrary accuracy.
